name: Kwararafa

summary.text: A multi-ethnic confederacy led by the Jukun in the Benue valley, rich from the salt flats of Awe and Keana. In the 17th century its cavalry raided Kano, Zaria, Katsina and even the Bornu capital. It declined in the 18th century, and the Jukun kingdom of Wukari carried on its name.

snapshots.title: A Benue valley power
snapshots.text: After defeats by Bornu in the late 15th century the capital moves to Biepi, near today's Ibi on the Benue. The confederacy controls the valley's salt.

snapshots.title: Raids across the north
snapshots.text: Kwararafa cavalry raid Kano (1650s and 1670s), Zaria and Katsina, and in 1680 reach Ngazargamu, the Bornu capital.
snapshots.note: Idoma and other Benue peoples trace origins to Kwararafa; whether it ruled them is debated.

snapshots.title: Decline; the court at Wukari
snapshots.text: Internal disputes and pressure from neighbours weaken the confederacy. The Jukun capital moves to Uka and then Wukari.

snapshots.title: Wukari between Muri and the Tiv
snapshots.text: The Fulani emirate of Muri takes the north of the old lands, and Tiv farmers expand from the south. Wukari remains a Jukun kingdom until British rule around 1900.

today.text: The Aku Uka, king of the Jukun, reigns at Wukari in Taraba State.
today.title: Aku Uka of Wukari

reviewNotes: Kwararafa's early capitals (Santolo, Pindiga, Tagara) are placed in different areas by different writers and are left off the map.
